newsitem.title: USA: Senate to subpoena White House for fund documents.
newsitem.headline: Senate to subpoena White House for fund documents.

text.p: The chairman of the U.S. Senate committee investigating campaign fund-raising scandals accused the White House on Wednesday of putting obstacles in his path and said he would issue subpoenas for all relevant documents this week.

"We have tried to work with the White House. We have tried to do it in private. We have tried to do it attorney to attorney in a responsible manner. They have not operated in good faith," Senate Governmental Affairs Committee Chairman Fred Thompson of Tennessee said.

Thompson exploded in anger after the White House waited until the end of a day of testimony about a controversial Asian businessman before producing records, sought by the committee for months, showing that the businessman visited the White House 10 times between 1994 and 1996.

Macau-based Ng Lap Seng, also known as Mr. Wu, provided nearly $1 million to Little Rock restaurateur Charlie Trie, $220,000 of which ended up as illegal foreign donations to the Democratic National Committee.
Thompson said the timing of the information, after the testimony was complete, had destroyed his faith in the White House.
"We are not going to tolerate that. Subpoenas have been prepared for all relevant documents," he said. The subpoenas had already been signed and would be issued later this week, he added.
